tools.name: deploy_html
tools.description: Deploy one HTML document and get back a live, unguessable https://<slug>.ship.place/ URL. Anonymous: 10 deploys/min per IP, 10MB body cap, 7-day expiry. Pro ($4/mo): custom or no TTL, named drops. Forms: a <form method="post"> with an email or phone field that posts to the page itself saves each res

tools.name: deploy_files
tools.description: Deploy a map of path -> content as a multi-file site (must include index.html to serve at the root). Anonymous: up to 100 files per request, 7-day expiry (30 days once signed in). Pro ($4/mo): up to 10,000 files, custom or no TTL, named drops. Forms: a <form method="post"> with an email or phone fie

tools.name: append_files
tools.description: Add files to a drop owned by the authenticated account (requires an sp_ API key and an active subscription): up to 10,000 files per drop in total, and existing paths are overwritten. The drop keeps its current expiry and password protection.

tools.name: list_drops
tools.description: List drops owned by the authenticated account (requires an sp_ API key; anonymous drops are not listable). Returns slug, url, name, file counts, expiry and password_protected, newest first.

tools.name: claim_drop
tools.description: Attach an anonymously deployed drop to the authenticated account using its one-time claim token (spc_..., returned once by deploy_html/deploy_files). Claiming a live drop extends it to the free-account lifetime (30 days). A drop that already expired can still be claimed, but it stays expired until i

tools.name: restore_drop
tools.description: Bring back an expired drop owned by the authenticated account, however long ago it expired (requires an sp_ API key on a paid plan). The restored drop doesn't expire while the account stays on Pro. Free accounts get a 402 subscription_required with an upgrade_url.

tools.name: delete_drop
tools.description: Permanently delete a drop owned by the authenticated account (requires an sp_ API key). The URL stops serving immediately and cannot be recovered.

tools.name: set_drop_password
tools.description: Set or rotate the shared password on a drop you own. Requires an sp_ API key and active paid Pro/Team; unavailable billing returns an error, not a public drop. Visitors unlock in their browser. Never put the password in a URL.

tools.name: remove_drop_password
tools.description: Remove password protection from a drop you own, making it readable by anyone with its URL. Requires an sp_ API key; works even after your paid subscription lapses.

tools.name: get_limits
tools.description: Show the ship.page plan matrix (anonymous free tier vs Pro $4/mo vs Team $19/mo) and, when an sp_ API key is present, the caller's current account/plan status.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show the authenticated account's plan, subscription status and usage (requires an sp_ API key). Anonymous callers should use get_limits for the static free-tier limits.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: deploy_html, list_drops · Private data: deploy_html, deploy_files, append_files, list_drops, claim_drop, restore_drop, delete_drop, set_drop_password, remove_drop_password, get_limits, get_account · Public sink: deploy_html, deploy_files · Destructive: deploy_html, deploy_files, append_files, claim_drop, restore_drop, delete_drop, set_drop_password, remove_drop_password.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: deploy_html, list_drops · Private data: deploy_html, deploy_files, append_files, list_drops, claim_drop, restore_drop, delete_drop, set_drop_password, remove_drop_password, get_limits, get_account · Public sink: deploy_html, deploy_files · Destructive: deploy_html, deploy_files, append_files, claim_drop, restore_drop, delete_drop, set_drop_password, remove_drop_password

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "deploy_html" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

Forms: a <form method="post"> with an email or phone field that posts to the page itself saves each res"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
